label: SpO₂
what: SpO₂ is below 94 %.
why: Low oxygen saturation can mean hypoxia from a cabin atmosphere fault, fire or smoke.
howDecided: Rule SPO-01: SpO₂ < 94 % → level 3, check. Earth clinical convention, not a NASA in-flight limit (health-indicators §4).
next: Re-measure: warm your hands, sit still for 1 minute, finger fully in, hand at heart level. Still below 94 % → tell the CMO now.

label: SpO₂
what: SpO₂ is below 90 %.
why: Low oxygen saturation can mean hypoxia from a cabin atmosphere fault, fire or smoke.
howDecided: Rule SPO-02: SpO₂ < 90 % → level 5, emergency. Earth clinical convention, not a NASA in-flight limit (health-indicators §4).
next: CMO now and notify ground.

label: PVT median
what: Your PVT median is above {limit} ms, {percent} % slower than your pre-flight baseline ({baseline} ms).
why: PVT slows early in flight in ISS crews, and nights of 6 h or less of sleep slow it further. Slower attention raises the risk of performance errors.
howDecided: Rule COG-01: PVT median > {limit} ms (pre-flight baseline {baseline} ms + {percent} %) → level 3, check. The baseline is a synthetic pre-loaded profile; +{percent} % is a team heuristic, not a NASA limit. No adaptation corridor yet.
next: Tell the CMO today and repeat the test tomorrow morning.

label: CO₂ (1-h avg)
what: Cabin CO₂ is above 3 mmHg as a 1-hour average.
why: CO₂ above the limit is linked to headaches in ISS crews (reported at 2.8–4.5 mmHg) and can add to fatigue and slower thinking.
howDecided: Rule CAB-01: CO₂ 1-h average > 3 mmHg → level 3, check. NASA-STD-3001 limit [V2 6004] (health-indicators §22).
next: Tell the CMO today and note any headache in your check-in. The CMO checks the cabin CO₂ trend with ground.

label: Cabin temp
what: Cabin temperature is below 18 °C.
why: NASA's health range for cabin temperature is 18–27 °C; outside it, heat or cold stress adds to fatigue and poor sleep.
howDecided: Rule CAB-02: cabin temp < 18 °C → level 3, check. NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 range 18–27 °C (health-indicators §22).
next: Tell the CMO today. The CMO checks cabin temperature control with ground.

label: Cabin temp
what: Cabin temperature is above 27 °C.
why: NASA's health range for cabin temperature is 18–27 °C; outside it, heat or cold stress adds to fatigue and poor sleep.
howDecided: Rule CAB-03: cabin temp > 27 °C → level 3, check. NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 range 18–27 °C (health-indicators §22).
next: Tell the CMO today. The CMO checks cabin temperature control with ground.

label: Cabin humidity
what: Cabin humidity is below 25 % RH.
why: NASA's health range for cabin humidity is 25–75 % RH; outside it, dry or damp air adds to discomfort and illness risk.
howDecided: Rule CAB-04: cabin humidity < 25 % RH → level 3, check. NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 range 25–75 % RH (health-indicators §22).
next: Tell the CMO today. The CMO checks cabin humidity control with ground.

label: Cabin humidity
what: Cabin humidity is above 75 % RH.
why: NASA's health range for cabin humidity is 25–75 % RH; outside it, dry or damp air adds to discomfort and illness risk.
howDecided: Rule CAB-05: cabin humidity > 75 % RH → level 3, check. NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 range 25–75 % RH (health-indicators §22).
next: Tell the CMO today. The CMO checks cabin humidity control with ground.

label: 30-day BFO dose
what: Your 30-day blood-forming-organ dose is above 125 mGy-Eq, half the 30-day limit.
why: Space radiation raises the risk of cancer and acute effects. The 30-day limit for blood-forming organs is 250 mGy-Eq.
howDecided: Rule RAD-01: 30-day BFO dose > 125 mGy-Eq → level 3, check. The 250 mGy-Eq limit is NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 (health-indicators §19); 50 % of it is a team heuristic, not a NASA level.
next: Tell the CMO today. The CMO reviews the dose trend and shielding with ground.

label: 30-day BFO dose
what: Your 30-day blood-forming-organ dose is above the 30-day limit of 250 mGy-Eq.
why: Space radiation raises the risk of cancer and acute effects. The 30-day limit for blood-forming organs is 250 mGy-Eq.
howDecided: Rule RAD-02: 30-day BFO dose > 250 mGy-Eq → level 5, emergency. NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 30-day limit for blood-forming organs (health-indicators §19).
next: CMO now and notify ground. If a radiation alarm sounds, go to the shelter.

label: Heart rate
what: Heart rate is above 100 bpm.
why: A resting heart rate above 100 bpm is tachycardia.
howDecided: Rule CV-01: heart rate > 100 bpm → level 3, check. Earth clinical convention for resting tachycardia, not a NASA in-flight limit (health-indicators §1).
next: Sit still for 5 minutes and re-measure. Still above 100 bpm → tell the CMO today.

label: Heart rate
what: Heart rate is below 40 bpm.
why: A heart rate below 40 bpm is bradycardia; with dizziness or fainting it needs attention.
howDecided: Rule CV-02: heart rate < 40 bpm → level 3, check. Earth clinical convention (bradycardia below 40–50 bpm with symptoms), not a NASA in-flight limit (health-indicators §1).
next: Re-measure. Still below 40 bpm, or dizzy → tell the CMO today.

label: Systolic
what: Systolic blood pressure is above 119 mmHg.
why: Blood pressure is drifting up from normal. In flight blood pressure usually drops, so a rise is unusual.
howDecided: Rule BP-01: systolic > 119 mmHg → level 2, watch. 2017 AHA "elevated" category, an Earth band that applies poorly in flight (health-indicators §3).
next: Re-measure tomorrow at the same time, seated and rested.

label: Systolic
what: Systolic blood pressure is above 129 mmHg.
why: Blood pressure is in the AHA stage 1 range.
howDecided: Rule BP-02: systolic > 129 mmHg → level 3, check. 2017 AHA stage 1, an Earth band that applies poorly in flight (health-indicators §3).
next: Re-measure after 5 minutes seated. Still high → tell the CMO today.

label: Diastolic
what: Diastolic blood pressure is above 79 mmHg.
why: Blood pressure is in the AHA stage 1 range.
howDecided: Rule BP-03: diastolic > 79 mmHg → level 3, check. 2017 AHA stage 1, an Earth band that applies poorly in flight (health-indicators §3).
next: Re-measure after 5 minutes seated. Still high → tell the CMO today.

label: Systolic
what: Systolic blood pressure is above 139 mmHg.
why: Blood pressure is in the AHA stage 2 range.
howDecided: Rule BP-04: systolic > 139 mmHg → level 4, treat. 2017 AHA stage 2, an Earth band that applies poorly in flight (health-indicators §3).
next: Re-measure now. Still high → CMO now and add it to today's medical conference.

label: Diastolic
what: Diastolic blood pressure is above 89 mmHg.
why: Blood pressure is in the AHA stage 2 range.
howDecided: Rule BP-05: diastolic > 89 mmHg → level 4, treat. 2017 AHA stage 2, an Earth band that applies poorly in flight (health-indicators §3).
next: Re-measure now. Still high → CMO now and add it to today's medical conference.

label: Systolic
what: Systolic blood pressure is above 179 mmHg.
why: Blood pressure is in the severe range.
howDecided: Rule BP-06: systolic > 179 mmHg → level 5, emergency. 2017 AHA severe ("crisis") definition, an Earth band (health-indicators §3).
next: CMO now and notify ground.

label: Diastolic
what: Diastolic blood pressure is above 119 mmHg.
why: Blood pressure is in the severe range.
howDecided: Rule BP-07: diastolic > 119 mmHg → level 5, emergency. 2017 AHA severe ("crisis") definition, an Earth band (health-indicators §3).
next: CMO now and notify ground.

label: Temperature
what: Body temperature is above 37.9 °C.
why: A fever can mean an infection. In flight resting core temperature runs about 1 °C higher, so an Earth cut-off may false-alarm.
howDecided: Rule TMP-01: body temperature > 37.9 °C → level 3, check. Earth fever cut-off of 38.0 °C, not a NASA in-flight limit (health-indicators §6).
next: Re-measure in 30 minutes and note any symptoms in your check-in. Still above 37.9 °C → tell the CMO today.

label: CO₂ (1-h avg)
what: Cabin CO₂ is above 2.5 mmHg as a 1-hour average.
why: Keeping CO₂ below 2.5 mmHg holds headache risk below 1 % in ISS crews.
howDecided: Rule CAB-06: CO₂ 1-h average > 2.5 mmHg → level 2, watch. 2.5 mmHg is a 7-day-average value applied to the 1-h average, a team heuristic (health-indicators §22).
next: Note any headache in your check-in.

label: Dose rate
what: Dose rate is above 0.9 mSv/day.
why: NASA designs habitats to keep the galactic cosmic ray dose rate below 0.9 mSv/day on surfaces.
howDecided: Rule RAD-03: dose rate > 0.9 mSv/day → level 3, check. NASA-STD-3001 [V1 4033] surface habitat design limit, not a crew exposure limit (health-indicators §19).
next: Tell the CMO today. The CMO checks the dose trend and shielding with ground.
